newsitem.title: USA: Lubrizol sees at least 4 pct volume growth.
newsitem.headline: Lubrizol sees at least 4 pct volume growth.

text.p: The Lubrizol Corp said Monday it expects sales to increase at least four percent in 1997 despite the negative impact of a stronger U.S. dollar and hurdles of a changing product mix and competitive pricing.

The company earlier reported operating earnings per share of $0.66 for the first quarter of 1997 versus $0.59 during the same period last year -- excluding a $34.6 million after-tax gain realized in the 1996 quarter from sales of investments.

"Overall, the first quarter was strong as operating earnings per share increased 12 percent despite a $.02 per share negative impact from the stronger U.S. dollar," said chief executive officer W.G. Bares.

"However, growth in consolidated revenues remained challenging as the effects of a changing product mix, competitive product pricing, the stronger U.S. dollar and the 1996 divestiture of our SVO operations offset the volume gains in our business," he added.

"These same factors will continue to make revenue growth a challenge in 1997," he said, but added, "we continue to believe we can deliver at least four percent volume growth and a 10 percent earnings per share increase in 1997."

Bares said shipments rose four percent in the United States and six percent in international markets during the first quarter of 1997, compared with a year ago -- with operating margins helped by favorable raw material costs.
